title: Regular alteration preserving a Cartier subboundary
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $B$ be a nonempty integral separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $\mathcal I,\mathcal J\subseteq\mathcal O_B$ be effective Cartier ideals [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal] with $V(\mathcal J)\subseteq V(\mathcal I)$. There exist a nonempty regular integral separated finite-type $k$-scheme $Y$ [def-weil-regular-scheme], a proper dominant $k$-morphism $a:Y\to B$ [def-weil-proper-morphism] inducing a finite extension $k(Y)/k(B)$ [def-sc-function-field, def-pc-field-extension], and a reduced strict normal crossings boundary $D=\bigcup_{i\in A}D_i$ on $Y$ [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary], with $A$ finite, such that the extended ideals $\mathcal I\mathcal O_Y$ and $\mathcal J\mathcal O_Y$ are effective Cartier and
$$V(\mathcal I\mathcal O_Y)=|D|,\qquad V(\mathcal J\mathcal O_Y)=\bigcup_{i\in A_{\rm out}}|D_i|$$
for some $A_{\rm out}\subseteq A$. In particular each of the two inverse-image complements is precisely the complement of the displayed support. Empty divisors, the unit ideal, and equal supports are allowed; no separability of $k(Y)/k(B)$ is required.

The latter uses literature/stacks-project/more-algebra.tex, Tag 0AG0 (lemma-regular-local-UFD). proof.text: The Cartier support misses the generic point: a local regular generator cannot vanish in a domain. Every nonempty open contains the generic point, so the support has empty interior. Choose the prime 2 or 3 different from the characteristic and apply [lem-sfb-gabber-global-snc-alteration]. Retain the proper surjection a0:P→B, regularity of P, the SNC inverse-image ideal D0, and the generic residue-field finiteness clause.

source.place: X Theorem 2.1, printed p.149; agent application to the Cartier support

proof.text: Properness over the finite-type base makes P finite type and quasi-compact over k, hence Noetherian. Regular stalks are integrally closed domains. Apply [rem-pc-regular-normal](2) to obtain finitely many clopen integral irreducible components. Surjectivity of a0 supplies a point and the open cover supplies a nonempty component Y. Its inclusion is both open and closed, hence proper, and stalk isomorphisms give regularity of Y. The generic-point clause of the alteration makes a:Y→B dominant. The open inclusion induces residue-field isomorphisms, so composition preserves the generic residue-field finiteness. The proved source lemma Scheme.Hom.finrank_stalk_eq_finrank_residueField identifies the finite positive generic residue degree with the degree of the canonical dominantFunctionFieldAlgebra, giving finiteness of that algebra. Composition gives the stated separatedness and finite-type conditions.

source.place: X Theorem 2.1; integral-component selection using Stacks 033M, 01T6 and proper closed inclusions

proof.text: Restrict D0 along the clopen inclusion f:Y→P. Any integral component meeting its clopen range lies wholly in it, by connectedness of its irreducible support. Index the surviving components by a finite subtype and enumerate it by Fin m. Pullbacks have nonempty integral subschemes because their maps to the original components are open immersions. Stalk isomorphisms give regularity. Their supports stay distinct because the original supports lie in the range of f. Restriction preserves the Cartier condition by flat pullback, and radicality by the affine appIso and Ideal.comap_radical. The support union equality follows from finite closed unions and preimages. For an intersection indexed by s, pullback commutes with the ideal sums, using the comap/map Galois connection. Its natural map to the original intersection is an open immersion, so stalk isomorphisms preserve regularity and the dimension equality. The injective reindexing preserves s.card. This checks the SNC boundary definition directly, including s empty; it uses no parameter criterion.

source.place: VIII Remark 4.2.2(i), printed pp.118--119; clopen restriction of X Theorem 2.1

proof.text: An invertible ideal on an integral scheme is nonzero. Its pullback along a dominant map of integral schemes is locally principal and nonzero: a zero pullback would imply the ideal is contained in the kernel of that map, while schematic dominance makes the kernel zero. The proved nonzero locally-principal criterion therefore makes both pulled-back ideals Cartier. Support-comap, support-radical and support-vanishingIdeal identify the first support with D and give containment of the second.

source.place: Integral-scheme generic-stalk calculation; agent local-generator argument (no flatness assumption)

proof.text: Select exactly the indices i with support(C_i) contained in the smaller support. For a point x of the smaller support, its stalk has positive dimension: dimension zero on an integral scheme forces x to be generic, whereas a Cartier support misses the generic point. Apply the already proved [lem-sbc-locally-principal-support-dimension-one] to find a generalization y in the same support with ambient stalk dimension one. The finite closed union covering D puts y in some C_i. Lift y to z on that integral component. The singleton-intersection dimension equality in the SNC predicate gives dim O_(C_i,z)=0, hence z is its generic point. Closedness of the smaller support then contains the whole C_i. Closedness of C_i and specialization y→x put x in the same selected component. This proves the equality with the selected finite union. This uses only the generic dimension-one detection lemma, not any smooth-base-change theorem or unit proof step.

source.place: Tags 0BJG and 0BJH, dimension-one detection for locally principal support; SNC singleton codimension and specialization give the subboundary consequence.

proof.text: Take complements of the support-comap and selected-union equalities to obtain the last two assertions. The argument allows empty supports and an empty family: if no component is selected then the same pointwise argument forces the smaller support empty. Unit ideals, equal supports, characteristic 2 and inseparable generic extensions require no separate assumptions.
